# Torn Utilities — User Agreement and Data Use Disclosure

Version: 1.4
Agreement number: 5
Effective date: 2026-11-11

## 1. About TU and Torn's rules

Torn Utilities (TU) is an independent third-party tool. Torn City does not
operate, endorse or certify TU. A feature being available in TU does not mean
Torn staff have approved that feature.

Your use of TU remains subject to [Torn's Rules](https://wiki.torn.com/wiki/Rules),
its scripting rules and the [Torn API terms](https://www.torn.com/api.html).
This agreement does not override those requirements or authorize prohibited
conduct. Stop using a feature if Torn staff instruct you to do so.

TU must use keys and information only for the purposes disclosed here and
permissions you have given. Material changes to purposes, recipients or access
requirements must be disclosed before the changed use begins.

## 2. API keys, access and required disclosures

TU never asks for your Torn password. Obtain your key directly from Torn and use
the least access needed for the features you choose. Registration accepts
**Public Only or Limited Access** keys. Full Access is not required or accepted
for registration. Providing a Limited Access key is not permission to retrieve
every selection available through that key.

TU verifies the key's access level and account owner with Torn. You should not
need to supply a name or player ID separately for verification. TU may retain
your verified Torn name and ID as described below. You may remove your
identifying information through Settings > API > Delete My TU Data, as
described in section 6.

The public Torn API is read-only. TU uses it for information requests. Supported
Snatch and Run item-use requests instead use your signed-in Torn website session
and Torn's security token. They are website gameplay actions, not writes through
the public API.

The following tables describe storage, recipients, purpose, key handling and
required access. The same information must be clearly visible at every place
TU asks you to provide a key. A hidden link alone does not replace that
key-entry disclosure.

### Account verification, TU access and agreement records

| Disclosure | Details |
|---|---|
| Data storage | TU stores verified identity, access permissions, agreement events, session metadata and audit records until cleared through the deletion process in section 6 or otherwise removed by the service. Delete My TU Data removes your identifying information from TU-controlled active storage and invalidates your TU access. Non-identifying service records may remain. Provider logs, backups and separately exported copies have the limits described in section 6. Expiry of access alone is not deletion. |
| Data sharing | You, authorized TU operators, Torn for verification, and hosting providers processing TU's service. Account and session records are not intended to be public records. |
| Purpose of use | Verify identity and access, maintain sessions, record agreement decisions and investigate abuse. |
| Key storage and sharing | Saved keys use the storage mode explained in section 3. Registration sends the selected key over HTTPS to TU's backend, which sends it to Torn for verification. The key is processed during verification; raw keys are not written to TU's application database. Provider logging is separate from application database behavior. |
| Required access / selections | Public Only or Limited Access; key information and public user identity selections. Full Access is not accepted for registration. |

### Travel Assistant and Item Monitor reads

| Disclosure | Details |
|---|---|
| Data storage | Settings, verified identity and feature caches are stored in your browser until cleared, replaced or expired by the feature. Delete My TU Data clears the selected account’s identity and credentials from this TU installation, including private manager storage and supported fallback copies. Non-identifying settings need not be erased. Other installations and exported copies are covered in section 6. |
| Data sharing | You and Torn. Reporting to TU is described separately below. |
| Purpose of use | Display item and price information; calculate travel and purchase capacity; check travel, hospital and inventory status; monitor availability. This supplies gameplay and competitive information, not a guarantee of availability or profit. |
| Key storage and sharing | The selected saved key is sent to Torn for enabled reads. Saving a key does not authorize publishing it or private API data to other players. |
| Required access / selections | Public profile and item catalog. Verified Limited Access for private travel, medical inventory and cooldown reads where used. Any item-market read must use the access allowed by Torn for its endpoint and version. |

### War Organizer and enabled player/faction features

| Disclosure | Details |
|---|---|
| Data storage | Settings, fetched information and feature caches may be retained locally until cleared or replaced. |
| Data sharing | You and Torn. A feature that shares a board or information must identify its recipients before sharing. |
| Purpose of use | Display player/faction information and organize targets or reservations for gameplay planning and competitive information. |
| Key storage and sharing | The selected feature key is sent to Torn for the requested read. A key's technical access is not consent to unrelated retrieval or disclosure. |
| Required access / selections | Only the supported faction-member, faction-snapshot and player-profile selections needed for the feature. Verified Limited Access is required where the feature uses it. Additional private selections must be disclosed before use. |

### Optional foreign-stock reporting and travel feedback

| Disclosure | Details |
|---|---|
| Data storage | TU keeps a bounded local history and pending upload queue. Accepted observations and feedback are stored remotely and may remain indefinitely. Delete My TU Data removes account-identifying links and related personal information; non-identifying stock observations, feedback and aggregate statistics may remain. Pending delivery is stopped when TU access is removed. |
| Data sharing | TU operators and hosting providers. Stock observations, history and derived estimates may be available to the general public. A submission's TU session allows the service to associate the request with a verified account; reporting is not represented as anonymous. |
| Purpose of use | Community stock history, depletion/restock estimates, travel planning and evaluation of forecasts. This provides gameplay information and a competitive advantage to users of that information. |
| Key storage and sharing | Stock and feedback payloads do not include a raw Torn API key. Authenticated delivery sends a TU session token to TU. Account identities and session tokens are not intended to be public fields in the stock data service. |
| Required access / selections | Reading the visible page for an observation requires no Torn API read. Authenticated submission requires TU registration, the relevant module permission and the current agreement. Any separate API reads use the access disclosed for their feature. |

### Security and request-limit counters

| Disclosure | Details |
|---|---|
| Data storage | Rate-limit counters hold timestamps and hashed key, account or IP identifiers as needed. The active windows are 70 seconds for registration and 60 seconds for submissions. Expired entries stop counting; scheduled cleanup removes expired counter entries when it runs. Identifying limiter state that TU can associate with your account is included in the deletion process. Provider logs and backups have the limits in section 6. |
| Data sharing | TU's service and hosting provider; authorized operators may access service state. These hashes are pseudonymous identifiers, not a promise of anonymity. |
| Purpose of use | Enforce service limits, reduce repeated failed verification and protect reporting/database capacity. |
| Key storage and sharing | Limiter state does not contain raw API keys or raw TU session tokens. Verification and authenticated requests still process their credentials as disclosed in the other rows. |
| Required access / selections | No additional Torn API access merely to maintain these counters. |

### Chat archives and local diagnostic reports

| Disclosure | Details |
|---|---|
| Data storage | Chat capture remains in the feature's local session until cleared or the session ends. Diagnostic histories use bounded local/session storage. Delete My TU Data removes your identifying information from TU-managed local caches and histories on this installation. It does not erase other players’ information generally or recall files you exported, copied or shared. Those copies remain wherever you saved or shared them. |
| Data sharing | You and any recipients you choose for an export. Enabling diagnostics does not itself authorize uploading a full diagnostic report or chat archive to TU. |
| Purpose of use | Your conversation archive, troubleshooting, development testing and support. |
| Key storage and sharing | Reports are designed to omit API keys, cookies, authentication headers and security-token values. They can still contain personal or gameplay information. Inspect reports before sharing; redaction is not a guarantee that every sensitive detail has been removed. |
| Required access / selections | No additional key for local capture of page information already available to you. Accompanying API reads use the access disclosed for their feature. |

### TU multiplayer games and shared results

| Disclosure | Details |
|---|---|
| Data storage | TU stores room activity, participant identifiers, session metadata and game records needed by the feature. Delete My TU Data removes your identifying information and account links and invalidates your room/session credentials. Results or history may remain only without personal information that identifies or reconnects them to you. Other players’ records are not deleted by your request. |
| Data sharing | TU operators and hosting providers; room participants and users of the applicable shared results or history. |
| Purpose of use | Operate TU multiplayer rooms, games, results and related community features. |
| Key storage and sharing | Games use TU sessions and room credentials. Raw Torn API keys are not sent to other players as game data. Registration is disclosed above. |
| Required access / selections | No additional Torn API access merely to play a TU multiplayer game. |

## 3. Local storage, TU sessions and confidentiality

**Supported userscript managers.** Where TU verifies support for synchronous
userscript-manager storage, saved keys are kept in that manager's private
storage rather than Torn-origin credential fields. TU copies and verifies
legacy credentials before removing their origin copies. This is storage
isolation, not encryption. Manager exports, sync and backups follow that
manager's settings and policies.

**PDA and unsupported environments.** Where verified private storage is not
available, TU uses unencrypted Torn-origin browser storage for saved keys.
Other scripts running on Torn pages may be able to read it. This fallback must
be identified in the key settings. If a supported private-storage migration or
write fails, TU must not silently switch those credentials to origin storage.
Existing data may be retained while the failure is resolved.

**TU session tokens.** A TU token is a credential for TU's service, distinct from
a Torn API key or Torn website session. In supported-manager mode,
TU session tokens also use verified private storage. Origin authorization and
identity caches use nonsensitive markers instead of token copies. PDA and
unsupported hosts retain an unencrypted origin-session-storage fallback.

Under the current configuration, TU sessions expire after no more than
24 hours unless revoked earlier; the server's expiry and account restrictions
remain authoritative. Expired private client records are removed when read or
cleared. TU does not promise a background deletion process for closed-tab or
orphaned records, manager backups or sync copies. The backend stores a hash of
the TU session token for authentication; expiry does not delete the historical
database row automatically.

**Page inputs and other caches.** A key you type, paste or reveal is present in
the page input and may be observable by other page scripts while displayed.
Private credential storage does not isolate every setting, exported file or
feature-data cache, and cannot protect against a compromised browser, extension,
userscript manager or device.

TU and its operators must protect keys and API-derived information, restrict
access to authorized purposes, and not sell, publish or repurpose your key or
private API data beyond the disclosures and permissions you have given.
Acceptance is not permission for unrelated uses.

Do not include keys, TU tokens or Torn security tokens in screenshots, public
issues or support messages. Remove saved keys in TU and revoke or replace them
in Torn if you no longer want them used or suspect exposure. Removing an individual saved key alone does not delete remote records. Use
Delete My TU Data for the account-identity deletion process in section 6.
Neither action recalls copies already exported or revokes a key at Torn.

## 4. Snatch and Run and user actions

Snatch and Run may monitor stock, calculate quantities, update clocks, sound
alerts, check inventory and interpret action results automatically. A stock
change or alarm does not authorize automatic item use, destruction, purchase
or travel.

Pressing the active action button requests the action displayed on it. Direct
item use consumes one selected supported item per press. Where a workflow needs
another Torn action step, TU displays that step and requires another user press.
An additional destruction or purchase transaction requires its own user action.
Information-only checks and status updates do not require an extra click or a
second TU popup acknowledging the same action.

Inventory destruction requires acceptance of its separate setup warning and
selection of the items to destroy. Actual destruction is permanent. TU must not
automatically replay an uncertain submitted gameplay action. A delayed message,
countdown or response alone does not prove success or failure; check Torn's
result before deciding what to do next.

After a confirmed purchase leaves inventory space, TU offers a choice: depart
through the step-by-step return flow, or close Snatch and Run and make additional
purchases and travel arrangements manually.

These are TU's intended action boundaries, not a claim of Torn approval for all
features. A website POST is still a gameplay action. Chat Archiver's
history-loading behavior and other modules must separately comply with Torn's
scripting rules.

## 5. Optional reporting and external services

Foreign-stock reporting is optional and off by default. When enabled on a
supported visible shop, it sends item identifiers, quantities, prices, country
and observation times to TU. Travel feedback may include the projection,
observed availability, quantities and relevant times you choose to submit.

The stock report body does not contain your name, player ID or raw API key.
However, delivery includes a TU session token, which lets TU verify and associate
the request with your account. Providers may also process IP addresses and
request metadata. Do not treat these submissions as anonymous.

Pending stock reports may be retained locally and retried while reporting is
enabled. Rate-limit or authorization failures pause delivery and leave reports
queued. Disabling reporting stops further automatic delivery while disabled;
it does not recall previously accepted reports. This reporting retry behavior
does not authorize retries of consumptive gameplay actions.

TU uses the following services for the stated purposes:

- **Torn:** API information, identity/key verification and user-requested website
  actions. [API terms](https://www.torn.com/api.html) and
  [Rules](https://wiki.torn.com/wiki/Rules).
- **Cloudflare:** hosting, request processing, databases and TU service
  infrastructure. [Terms](https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/) and
  [Privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/).
- **GitHub:** script distribution, updates and published agreement files.
  [Terms](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service)
  and [Privacy statement](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement).
- **YATA:** the TU backend may automatically retrieve public travel-stock
  information to supplement observations and estimates. This is a backend
  source-data integration; it does not require sending your registration key
  to YATA. [YATA website](https://yata.yt/).

Automatic integrations must remain within the purposes disclosed here. An
additional optional service integration must identify its data use and
recipients, provide its applicable terms link and obtain opt-in before it is
enabled. TU operators must follow applicable provider and source-data conditions.

Providers can process IP addresses, request timing, browser/platform information
and operational logs under their policies. Application database behavior does
not establish what provider logs or backups retain. TU must not promise log
redaction, deletion periods or operator-access controls that have not been
verified in the deployed service.

Stock observations, forecasts and market information may be inaccurate, disputed
or delayed. Authentication and duplicate/conflict checks do not prove a reported
observation is true. Predictions do not guarantee stock, purchase success or
profit.

## 6. Retention, deletion and your choices

You may decline this agreement, disable optional reporting, stop TU modules,
remove an individual saved key, delete your identifying information or uninstall
TU. These are different actions. Removing a saved key, uninstalling the script
or revoking a key at Torn does not, by itself, erase TU's server-held records.

### Delete My TU Data

Use **Settings > API > Delete My TU Data** to remove your personal identifying
information from TU. TU displays the scope and asks you to confirm before it
submits the deletion request. This is a self-service process. Ownership
verification protects other users' information; deleting your
own data must not require accepting a new agreement merely to request deletion.

The deletion scope is your selected, verified account. It includes:

- API keys saved by TU for that account on this installation, including supported
  private manager storage, fallback storage and legacy credential copies;
- your TU registration name and Torn player ID, registration/key-derived
  faction/account identity fields, and associated TU session and room credentials;
- identity links in agreement, access, audit, submission, feedback, multiplayer
  and other TU records, including identifying hashes or pseudonymous links that
  still allow TU to associate a retained record with you.

TU's registration service processes a raw API key to verify ownership; it does
not write raw registration keys to its application database. Deletion removes
the supported saved copies and associated account-derived identifying records
from this installation and active TU service storage. It
is not a statement that the server previously stored a raw API key.

This is an identity-data deletion action, not a general reset of all TU data.
Non-identifying preferences, public item/stock observations, aggregate statistics
and de-identified service or game records may remain. TU must not call retained
information de-identified if a remaining name, player ID, key hash, token or
other link still associates it with you. Your request does not delete other
players' personal records or change your Torn account, inventory or items.

Information obtained independently through other users’ APIs, other player
submissions or independent sources remains even when it mentions you. This
includes independently supported faction, player-status and activity observations.
Where a mixed record contains your own registration or submission attribution,
TU removes that attribution while preserving the independent information.

If TU cannot establish the owner of a legacy saved key, verify or remove that
saved key before proceeding. Cleanup can take over a minute while temporary
service-limit records expire. A pending recovery process temporarily retains
the minimum account and revoked-token linkage required to finish cleanup; it
is removed before completion is confirmed. Keep the originating installation
and use **Resume TU data deletion** if the process is interrupted.

### Confirmation, access removal and returning to TU

TU stops active tools and pending reporting during deletion. It displays a
**deletion-complete confirmation only after server deletion and the local
cleanup have been confirmed**. If either part fails or remains uncertain, TU
shows that status and a retry/recovery route rather than claiming completion.

Deletion removes your TU access and invalidates your TU sessions, including
sessions on other devices. Previously saved acceptance cannot restore access.
To use TU again, you must provide an API key again, complete fresh account
verification and explicitly accept the current user agreement. TU must not
silently restore removed credentials from a legacy cache or reuse an old
agreement record. Providing a key again does not automatically re-enable
optional reporting or other integrations that require separate consent.

Deleting information from TU does not revoke or delete the API key at Torn.
Revoke or replace it in Torn if you want to stop its use by other tools or if
you suspect exposure. Do not send credentials or private reports to a public
repository issue.

### Other copies and provider limits

The local cleanup applies to the TU installation where you perform the action.
Other browsers, devices, userscript-manager backups or sync copies can retain
local information. Their TU sessions become invalid, but their saved local
copies may require separate cleanup on those installations.

Files you exported, screenshots you saved and copies you shared are outside
this button's reach. TU cannot recall a recipient's copy. Torn, Cloudflare,
GitHub and other providers can retain their own operational logs or historical
backups under their policies. Active TU data deletion does not promise immediate
erasure from third-party logs, backups or systems TU cannot directly control.
TU must not report a broader deletion scope than the implemented process can
verify.

## 7. Responsible use and limitations

Do not use TU to evade Torn's rules, obtain another person's private information
without permission, bypass TU authorization or service limits, interfere with
other users or extract credentials. Restrictions on TU-hosted service use,
redistribution or modification remain subject to applicable permissions,
licenses and law, including permitted security research and other protected
rights.

TU must minimize requested data, respect Torn's API limits and stop using
invalid or disabled keys when the relevant error is received. The Torn API documentation states limits of **100 requests per minute per user
across keys** and **5,000 per minute per service IP**. Torn may change those
limits. Additional keys or servers do not authorize bypassing them.

TU's browser and backend safeguards cover their own defined request paths.
Other tools and keys on the same account, and other services sharing an outbound
IP, may also contribute to the applicable limit. TU does not claim its counters
control all such traffic.

TU is provided as-is. Features, third-party services and Torn responses can
change or fail. No agreement wording makes a defective or prohibited action
compliant. These terms do not limit rights that applicable law does not allow
to be waived.

## 8. Acceptance and changes

By selecting Accept on a published version, you acknowledge the disclosed
processing and agree to use TU subject to Torn's rules. TU records acceptance
against your verified account and the agreement version. Account-identity
deletion removes that account’s identifying acceptance link; returning requires
fresh acceptance. Acceptance does not
automatically enable optional reporting or another integration requiring
separate consent.

A new published agreement version requires renewed acceptance before continued
use of features that require it. Materially different key/data uses must not
begin under an old acceptance.
